notes: Located the site from the plan's own features: the protected, fenced area north-west of Kalibangan village holds two eroded mounds separated by a low north-south strip with a foot track. The western mound (about 140 m by 250 m, divided by an east-west saddle) is the citadel KLB-1 and the larger eastern mound is the lower city KLB-2; the sizes, the saddle at the citadel's partition wall and the straight excavation trench in KLB-2 all agree with the plan. Current imagery (Vantor Vivid 20260301) has no zoom-19 tiles; seven Wayback releases were compared and release 16749 (Vivid, 4 March 2021) was used for most points because the trenches and tracks are sharpest there; release 8432 (Vivid, 8 February 2019) shows the eroded relief best and has the same pixel frame (tile ranges identical, building corners agree to within 1 px). Capture dates come from each release's Wayback metadata layer (SRC_DATE2, read as month/day/year). Most surviving features are mound edges, so nearly all points are class C. The fitted plans make the citadel slightly larger than the mound seen in the imagery and the lower-city mound extends about 30 m beyond the drawn east wall, to the plan's outer contour. Seen without opening any file: the session's starting git status, and a later `git status` run to confirm which files I had written, list untracked conjecture files whose names state working hypotheses about town orientation (knowledge/conjectures/C-0015-towns-laid-out-on-star-settings.md and C-0016-plains-cities-on-true-north.md). They give no value for any plan, and I chose no point with them in mind.
